A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UIBDiffusion and provide readable main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A.1-A.10. The substantial layout change does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original backdoor experiments on CIFAR-10 and CelebA-HQ, defense evaluations, and additional NCSN results and ablations in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including attack success, generation quality, defense evasion and appendix ablation results.

M1.justification: Both retain the same classifier-guided trigger generator, additive and spatial perturbation optimization, and VillanDiffusion-based backdoor injection. Algorithms 1-2 and the generator architecture in Appendix A.9 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use CIFAR-10 and CelebA-HQ with the same targeted image-generation scenarios, including HAT, SHOE and CAT targets. No dataset, domain or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain BadDiffusion, VillanDiffusion and original UAP triggers, together with Elijah and TERD defenses. Newly cited defense papers are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and A.2-A.4 retain the same metrics, poisoning levels, training budgets, sampler settings, evaluation sample counts and defense procedures. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Both retain the trigger-generation comparison, imperceptibility measurements, inversion visualizations and analyses varying targets, guiding classifiers, trigger strength, poisoning rate and training epochs. Appendix relocation and resizing do not change these analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The matched tables and graphics retain the same results. Both report 100% UIBDiffusion versus 56% VillanDiffusion ASR at 5% poisoning in Section 4.2, and 82% ASR for UIBDiffusion on NCSN at 98% poisoning in Table 7.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives and clean/backdoor diffusion derivations in Sections 3.2-3.3 and Appendix A.7 are retained. Equations 1-18 undergo typesetting changes without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The rewritten contribution bullets retain the same first-imperceptible-attack claim, UAP adaptation, universality, utility and defense-evasion claims. The abstract and conclusion preserve their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The distribution-shift explanation, resistance-to-inversion interpretation, higher poisoning requirement for NCSN, and societal-impact discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Checkpoint identifiers, NVIDIA L40S hardware, appendix hyperparameters, defense implementation settings and generator details are retained. Both versions still promise a future release of triggers and code.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Anti-backdoor Learning, Adversarially Robust Anti-backdoor Learning, Neural Cleanse and Neural Attention Distillation in the introductory motivation; Diff-cleanse and PureDiffusion disappear. The main positioning relative to UAP/GUAP and diffusion backdoor research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes and rewrites the contribution bullets, adds equal-contribution and corresponding-author notes, and makes limited wording and reference-style edits. The main section and appendix ordering is retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column formatting, extensively resizing and relocating existing figures and tables. For example, Figures 18-19 move from separate full pages to adjacent columns on one page. Their underlying content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The method, experimental support, derivations and reproducibility information remain unchanged. v3 makes modest contribution-wording and citation refinements and adopts a more compact layout, which also shrinks several tables and appendix sample grids. These presentation tradeoffs leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
